races.name: Oktoberfest 3rd And 10th October Maiden Fillies' Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Delighfully Hot
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner who has led in three of four starts including a placed effort on Standard Southwell, but has yet to win and has been beaten by rivals who raced prominently behind her; the three-way pace battle today is the single biggest threat to her chances.

runners_data.name: Estupenda
runners_data.note: South African-trained filly with an OR=120 that dwarfs most of these rivals on official ratings, returning off a 124-day break for Joey Ramsden with an inexperienced 3lb claimer aboard; her sole run on Standard Southwell was a fifth, but class could tell if the pace scenario sets up perfectly.

runners_data.name: Kokumi
runners_data.note: Twice a runner-up on Good going for a lightly raced profile that leaves her somewhat unexposed; Dr Newland & Insole have had a quiet 14-day spell and the step to fibresand is genuinely untested, but her proximity at the line in both runs suggests she stays competitive.

runners_data.name: Quiet Soul
runners_data.note: Sean Levey takes over for Michael Herrington, whose yard has sent out three winners in the past 14 days, and Quiet Soul's best effort was a second on Standard Southwell — the one surface that genuinely suits her hold-up style; 45 days off is manageable and the pace scenario here is almost ideal for a horse who comes late.

runners_data.name: Sayidah Dubawi
runners_data.note: James Tate has placed four from 18 runners in the past fortnight and Billy Loughnane is a high-quality booking; no public form and running style genuinely unknown, which makes her the race's biggest wildcard and dangerous in any scenario if she shows superior raw ability.

runners_data.name: Sioux Moon
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes filly who has placed on both starts on Good ground, showing she handles a quick surface; a hold-up runner over 5f on fibresand for the first time, she will need the contested pace to materialise exactly as expected to arrive in time over this minimum trip.

runners_data.name: Viking Barbie
runners_data.note: Front-runner with the most fibresand experience in this field — one placed effort from five starts on Standard — and Marco Ghiani will look to use draw and early pace to control matters; the challenge is three horses chasing the same position, and any scrimmaging at the break will compromise her chance.

runners_data.name: Beautiful Effort
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is a positive booking and her best form has come on fibresand (second on Standard Southwell), suggesting the surface suits; naturally prominent, she will try to sit just behind the three leaders rather than get embroiled in the pace battle, which is the most sensible tactical position available.

runners_data.name: Chiwara
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey operation with a strong 14-day record of seven winners from 47 runs; a hold-up type who placed second on Good over 6f, she steps down to 5f on fibresand after 60 days off, and the strong pace suits but the trip reduction is a mild query over whether she can quicken sharply enough at the death.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Mystery
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's filly has an unsatisfactory recent form string including an unseated-rider incident, but her second on Good fibresand shows ability; Luke Morris will press for the front, but racing against two other confirmed front-runners on a flat 5f means she must win the early duel to have any chance of controlling the race.

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — Cosmic Mystery, Delighfully Hot, and Viking Barbie — will contest the lead from the break on this straight Southwell fibresand 5f, guaranteeing a strong, pressured gallop with no respite. Cosmic Mystery (Luke Morris, Archie Watson) and Viking Barbie (Marco Ghiani) have both shown front-running tendencies across multiple runs, while Delighfully Hot has led in three of her four outings, meaning none will willingly concede the rail. With the pace distributed across three horses burning early energy, the sectionals will be compressed in the first two furlongs and the field will string out rapidly, leaving those who over-commit at the front vulnerable inside the final furlong. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent runners with a strong late kick — specifically Quiet Soul, Sioux Moon, and Chiwara — who can track the scramble from a covered position and pick up the pieces as the three leaders empty.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the three-way battle for the lead between Cosmic Mystery, Delighfully Hot, and Viking Barbie burns them all out before the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: The contested gallop drains the leaders early, and the race opens up in the final furlong for horses arriving fresh off the pace; hold-up runners who have conserved energy profit most because the front rank has nothing left to give.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners — most likely Viking Barbie or Cosmic Mystery — gets a soft lead after a brief skirmish and the others back off.
scenarios.body: A single pacesetter finds a comfortable rhythm and builds an unassailable gap before the closers can get competitive; on Standard Southwell fibresand, a horse that controls its own tempo on the front end can be exceptionally hard to reel in over 5f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the pace holds together long enough for a prominent tracker — Estupenda or Beautiful Effort — to latch onto the leaders' coat-tails and quicken past the flagging front trio in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: A prominent horse with more tactical speed than the hold-up brigade benefits from sitting just behind the battle, avoiding the worst of the fight, then sweeping through as the leaders tie up; Estupenda's OR=120 suggests class capable of exploiting this window.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets Market
scenarios.trigger: If a lightly raced or debutante type — Sayidah Dubawi or Kokumi — produces a step forward in form that the market has underestimated.
scenarios.body: Lightly raced fillies with unexposed profiles can surprise in maiden company when the pace is honest and the field becomes ragged; Sayidah Dubawi's unknown style leaves her profile genuinely open, and Kokumi's consecutive placed efforts on Good suggest untapped ability on a different surface.

watchPoints.text: If Cosmic Mystery and Delighfully Hot collide or bump at the break, both could be compromised before a stride has been run — watch the early stalls exit closely given three horses targeting the same space.

Quiet Soul's chance is entirely dependent on the pace being genuinely strong throughout; if Viking Barbie or Cosmic Mystery manages to steal a soft lead, the hold-up horses including Sioux Moon and Quiet Soul may find the race run too tamely to close.

Estupenda's OR=120 is strikingly high for maiden company but she is returning off a 124-day absence with an apprentice jockey — if she needs the run to strip fit, her class advantage evaporates quickly over a flat 5f.

Sayidah Dubawi is a complete unknown — no public form, style listed as unknown — and Billy Loughnane's booking could represent market support or simply a jockey filling a spare ride; monitor the market move closely before the off.

Standard fibresand at Southwell on a flat 5f track rewards horses that settle quickly behind the pace rather than those that fight for position; any runner that over-races in the opening furlong due to the three-way scramble is unlikely to finish off strongly.

races.name: Book The Bistro In Seasons Restaurant Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Edwardtheninth
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back wins over this course and distance on Standard give it strong form credentials, but 64 days off is notable and its natural hold-up style means it will likely be further back than ideal in a field crowded with closers, softening its chance in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Edwardtheninth shaped well when third last time out, and a winner two starts back, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; the chief concern is a 64-day absence leaving his fitness on trust.

runners_data.name: Lednikov
runners_data.note: Headgear-free and trained by Ivan Furtado who is 0/12 in the last 14 days, this veteran hold-up performer steps back up in trip — his best form is over further — but his true rear-of-field running style is compromised by the volume of closers in this race and he must race more forwardly than he would prefer.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a string of mid-field finishes, Lednikov is hard to fancy from sixth in the ratings, though he returns on a quick turnaround, has run over today's trip and going before, and his most recent effort — a third — at least shows some residual ability.

runners_data.name: Blue Tulip
runners_data.note: A three-year-old fitted with a hood, Billy Loughnane in the saddle for a trainer firing at 2/15 over the last fortnight; won over 1m4f on Standard and is tried over further here, with the trip extension a genuine question mark, though the going suits.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win two starts back before slipping to third last time out, Blue Tulip has experience of today's going and returns on a sharp 16-day turnaround, though her overall recent consistency is mixed and a middle ranking of five from seven tells its own story.

runners_data.name: Sound Gloria
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's three-year-old has a straightforward prominent style that should see Ray Dawson slot in just behind the leader without a fight; form figures include a win at 1m4f on Good and a placed effort at 1m6f, making this trip viable, but no wins on Standard AW surfaces is a minor flag.
runners_data.comment: Sound Gloria arrives in fine form, second last time out following a win two starts back, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — the chief question is whether 133 lb proves too much to overcome.

runners_data.name: Be Hopeful
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, ridden by Sean Levey for David Menuisier who is 0/11 in the last 14 days; all three runs to date are on Standard AW and all have produced defeats, though racing alone on the lead at 1m6f is a very different proposition to his previous roles — the key unknown is whether his modest form reflects ability or circumstance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Be Hopeful faces a stiff task off 130 lb with an official mark of 55, though he has run over today's going before and 26 days between runs leaves him fresh enough.

runners_data.name: Le Rouge Chinois
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the ride on this course specialist who has twice placed at 1m6f on Standard here; fitted with a hood, 14 days since last run, and the 10-runner record of 0 wins but 4 places tells a consistent but frustrating story — must convert proximity into a finish this time.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in his last two outings with back-to-back seconds, Le Rouge Chinois arrives on a sharp 14-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going, and his rating of 69 just edges this field of seven.

runners_data.name: Tropical Talent
runners_data.note: Returning from a massive 451-day absence which dominates this runner's profile and is impossible to ignore; all his best form is on Good ground and over this trip, which counts in his favour, but the AW surface at Southwell is unproven for him and a horse off over a year needs everything to go perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and off the track for 451 days, Tropical Talent has questions to answer on fitness, yet his going experience and a our rating of 67 — well clear of his official mark — suggest he retains more ability than recent form implies; returning to full fitness is the obvious risk.

races.paceDynamic: Be Hopeful is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead in a seven-runner field, Sean Levey will dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over 1m6f on Standard Fibresand at Southwell. Sound Gloria (P) and Tropical Talent (P) will press for the prominent slots behind the leader, creating a modest but organised pace that is unlikely to collapse into a sprint finish — the trip and surface combination almost guarantee a relatively even tempo throughout. Le Rouge Chinois, Blue Tulip, Edwardtheninth and Lednikov are all natural hold-up horses, and with multiple closers needing to close from varying positions, the race shape consistently rewards those who can travel within striking distance of the pace rather than those relying on a late surge from deep. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can honestly accommodate at the rear — Edwardtheninth and Lednikov, though true hold-up horses, are mapped to midfield because the cluster of closers cannot all race from their ideal position; Le Rouge Chinois, with proven form at this track and trip, is best placed to secure a genuine prominent hold-up berth behind the front two. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or just-off-the-pace profile — something that can track Be Hopeful within a couple of lengths and pounce before the true closers can reel in the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Be Hopeful Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Be Hopeful is allowed a soft lead at a measured tempo and the prominent horses cannot overhaul a relaxed front-runner.
scenarios.body: Be Hopeful gets a dream lead on a flat, tight circuit, conserves energy through the early stages, and has enough fuel to hold on as the closers fail to close the gap in time; at 1m6f on Standard going, a horse that settles well in front can be very hard to peg back when the pace is honest but not suicidal.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just honest enough to set up a perfectly-timed challenge from a close tracker in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Sound Gloria or Le Rouge Chinois, tracking within a length or two of Be Hopeful, makes a smooth move turning for home and reels in the leader before the true hold-up horses can land a blow; both have strong recent course or trip profiles at this level.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Gets Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If Be Hopeful sets a surprisingly strong gallop that strings out the field and leaves a genuine late gap for a finishing horse.
scenarios.body: Blue Tulip, stepping up in trip, or Lednikov — if able to secure a better position than mapped — benefits from a fast-run race where the front two tire; however, most of the true hold-up types are crowded at the rear and the Standard surface at Southwell does not often reward deep closers at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runners Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected rival pushes Be Hopeful into an unsustainable pace, leaving the whole field to unwind from midfield.
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace rivalry anticipated this is a low-probability scenario, and the horses who would benefit — Edwardtheninth and Lednikov — are operating out of their ideal positions and carry a style-fit discount that further reduces their chances in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Tropical Talent's 451-day layoff is the single biggest risk flag in the race — watch whether Harry Russell sends him forward early to get cover, or whether the fitness deficit forces a conservative ride that leaves him unable to land a blow.

Be Hopeful has failed to win in three attempts on Standard AW — watch whether Sean Levey rides for a soft lead or whether any early pressure from Sound Gloria or Tropical Talent forces a stronger gallop than anticipated, fundamentally changing the race shape.

Le Rouge Chinois has four places from ten runs on this course and trip combination but no win — watch whether De Sousa positions him closer than usual to try to convert place form into a victory, as his hood and consistent profile suggest he is vulnerable to a tactical switch.

Sound Gloria represents Roger Varian without a Southwell AW win on her record — if she fails to press the leader in the early stages and drifts back into the pack, the shape becomes very one-dimensional and Be Hopeful's chance improves significantly.

Edwardtheninth won here over 1m6f on Standard twice recently — watch the market to see whether punters take a strong view on whether 64 days off has left the horse fresh or ring-rusty, as its form at this exact track and trip is the strongest in the field on paper.

races.name: Winter Ladies Evening Sat 28th November Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Faeberon
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Standard here recently and is firmly in the mix as a handy prominent type; Jack Mitchell rode a cool race last time and the step up to 1m3f on this track suits the style, with no going concerns and headgear flag noted.
runners_data.comment: Faeberon returns after 23 days in good heart, a winner two starts back and third last time out, and he has experience of both today's trip and going. Carrying 132 lb from stall one, his rating of 80 marks him as the one to beat in this field of eight.

runners_data.name: Saxophonist
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning, placing five times from recent starts, but all form comes on Good ground so this Standard Fibresand surface is the key unknown; a hold-up approach means he needs more pace than New Bay Star is likely to inject.
runners_data.comment: Saxophonist has been a model of consistency, finishing second twice in his last two starts and placing in four of his last five, and he has run over today's trip and going before, making him a genuine danger at 131 lb; the concern is that he remains winless in recent starts and may find one too good again.

runners_data.name: New Bay Star
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who sets the entire shape of this race; Alistair Rawlinson can dictate every yard on this flat track and recent form shows he handles Standard Fibresand, though his last win is elusive and rivals will be watching for any signs of vulnerability in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, New Bay Star makes for a tough sell despite the experience over today's trip and going; the recent unplaced effort after consecutive placed runs is a concern, and 131 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: Golspie
runners_data.note: Solid course and distance form on Standard going with 12 runs in that context — this is clearly his track — but his true running style is that of a hold-up horse who will find himself racing further forward than he would like given the traffic at the rear; Patrick Morris has a live runner here on form alone, but the tactical displacement tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without being a winner, Golspie has finished third three times in recent starts yet remains winless, and while he has run over today's trip and going before, a career-high 129 lb from stall five is a stiff ask for a gelding rated 62 officially.

runners_data.name: Pace Attack
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's record with horses placed carefully into handicaps demands respect, and 14 days since last run keeps him fresh; however his natural instinct is to come from off the pace, and with the rear of the field crowded, Luke Morris will need to manufacture a clear run that may not materialise at the trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Pace Attack is hard to fancy despite the fitness edge of a 14-day turnaround, some going experience, and a handy draw at stall two.

runners_data.name: Carwyn
runners_data.note: The form figures are stark — nines and eights dominate the recent record — and a pattern of fading in the finish is a genuine structural concern; by nature a hold-up horse displaced further forward on the map than comfortable, and Barry McHugh faces a significant challenge to get a tune out of this one.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Carwyn at least has experience of today's trip and conditions, and 35 days between runs gives connections time to find a spark; however, a sequence of unplaced efforts makes him a difficult case to enthuse about from stall eight off 119 lb.

runners_data.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners_data.note: Carries top weight on 142lbs but has recent course and going form including a win over 10f on Good; the prominent style suits this race perfectly given the lack of pressure on the leader, and Liam Wright's 3lb claim partially offsets the burden.
runners_data.comment: Everyoneknowsadave catches the eye on the strength of a win two starts back and a placed effort three starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going; the concern is that fourth last time out suggests he needs to bounce back to his best.

runners_data.name: Bearwith
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with two wins from 15 runs on Standard going, including a recent victory; Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claim) aboard a genuinely hold-up horse who will be at the back of a crowded rear, making his route to the winner's enclosure dependent on a pace scenario that this race is unlikely to produce.
runners_data.comment: Bearwith shaped well when runner-up last time out and landed a win two starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going to call on; the risk is that ninth three starts back hints at some inconsistency to overcome.

races.paceDynamic: New Bay Star is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push her, she should be allowed to stride into an uncontested lead from the outset on this flat Fibresand circuit at Southwell. Faeberon and Everyoneknowsadave are legitimate prominent racers who will sit close behind, creating a compact, organised front group but one that is unlikely to press New Bay Star into a genuinely searching gallop. The remainder of the field — including Golspie, Pace Attack and Carwyn — are true hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is saturated with their type; none of them will be racing from their natural position, and that compromises their ability to deliver a telling late challenge. This race shape — one uncontested leader, a sustainable medium pace, and a prominent/pressing pack behind — strongly favours horses who can sit handy and press forward in the straight, making early movers from the prominent group the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: New Bay Star Dictates Freely
scenarios.trigger: If New Bay Star is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and controls the tempo throughout, the race becomes a test of which prominent horse can sustain a run into the straight.
scenarios.body: New Bay Star sets an uncontested, metronomic gallop and the race's outcome is settled in the home turn as Faeberon and Everyoneknowsadave pick up approaching the final two furlongs; the hold-up horses, already displaced from their natural positions, have too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Take Over
scenarios.trigger: If Faeberon or Everyoneknowsadave push forward earlier than expected and collectively lift the tempo in the final half mile, wearing down New Bay Star.
scenarios.body: New Bay Star's lead is eroded entering the final bend and the two prominent types sweep past to fight it out; the compressed gallop suits horses who can quicken off a decent clip from a handy position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to open the race up in the final furlong, enabling a closing run from the rear of the field.
scenarios.body: Bearwith, who has the strongest closing form figures of the hold-up horses and genuine Standard-going course credentials, would be the most likely beneficiary; Saxophonist, consistent in defeat, could also sustain a late rattle but both face a disadvantaged position given the field is loaded with hold-up types.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Strung Out
scenarios.trigger: If New Bay Star goes too hard early and stops suddenly, creating carnage through the field and throwing the race open to opportunists.
scenarios.body: An unlikely but plausible chaos scenario where those sitting just off the pace — Faeberon, Everyoneknowsadave — inherit a momentum advantage while the genuine closers remain too far back; the race becomes messy and the winner emerges from whoever is most adaptable tactically.

watchPoints.text: New Bay Star's early gallop sets the entire shape — watch for how hard Alistair Rawlinson pushes in the first three furlongs; if she is allowed to coast, the race will be settled by the home turn.
Everyoneknowsadave's 142lbs top weight could become significant in the final furlong over 1m3f — watch whether the weight tells as the race enters its business end.
Golspie and Bearwith are both genuine hold-up types operating out of their natural position in a rear that is overloaded; if they get hampered or boxed in early, they have little recourse.

Pace Attack's trainer Sir Mark Prescott has six runners from 16 in the last 14 days — a busy, confident yard — but watch whether the horse can find any position forward enough to land a challenge given the redistribution issue.

Carwyn's pattern of fading finishes is worth monitoring as a race-in-running signal; if he drops away sharply from the home turn, it confirms the pace scenario has not suited the hold-up brigade at all.

races.name: Festive Fixtures At Southwell Racecourse Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Portman Blue
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid Southwell form (8/8 visits on similar going) but a flat recent run string and 32-day absence; relies on pace collapsing ahead, which looks unlikely given the controlled shape this race will produce.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Portman Blue has form figures that make for grim reading, though he has run over today's distance and going before and draws stall one carrying 133 lb; our rating edges above his official mark, offering a sliver of hope for a long-overdue improvement.

runners_data.name: Izzari
runners_data.note: True closer whose best recent form over 8f on good ground contrasts with a patchy fibresand record (1W1P from 15 similar-going runs); the 20-day turnaround is fine but the map shape leaves him needing pace that simply may not be there.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and carrying strong fitness into this, Izzari has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 67 marks him out as a genuine threat from stall 14; the risk is that he remains winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Peaceful Spirit
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with only 3 runs on similar going and none of them placing; Rawlinson is capable but this filly's form line is thin and the style mismatch in a front-runner-controlled race is a clear concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, including a sixth last time out, Peaceful Spirit faces an uphill task from stall nine carrying 132 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 64 offers a sliver of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Aspull
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by nature whose best work comes from well off the pace, but with the rear of this field congested Phil McEntee's runner is mapped into midfield and will race out of its preferred position; limited fibresand experience (1 run on similar going) adds further doubt.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Aspull is hard to fancy from stall five off 131 lb, though he has run over today's trip before and a rating of 64 suggests he retains some ability — ninth of fourteen in the rankings, he arrives fresh enough on a nine-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Just Typical
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with Williams's yard 2/26 over 14 days — not a stable flying by numbers; Loughnane takes over and the horse has a plausible record at 8f on fibresand-style surfaces with three places from five comparable runs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Just Typical does bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third two starts back hints at some ability, though he has looked held most recently; 131 lb from stall 12 adds little encouragement for a horse ranked midfield in this field.

runners_data.name: Avatar Jet
runners_data.note: Won over this C&D trip on standard going and has placed twice more at 8f on similar surfaces, giving him meaningful course form; Wheatley tracks from off the pace and the horse could benefit if a gap opens in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Avatar Jet arrives fit on a 12-day turnaround, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating puts him as the top-ranked runner in the field — the worry is that he has been fifth and seventh in his last two starts, so he must find improvement.

runners_data.name: Volto di Medusa
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner in the race; Fallon on board and winning twice over 8f at Southwell on standard is a clear positive, though the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that at OR 64 he will be pulling more weight than rivals if his natural lead role is fully conceded.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to land a win four starts back, but has been inconsistent since, finishing unplaced and seventh before a solid second last time out; has run over today's trip and going, and 32 days between runs leaves his freshness an open question.

runners_data.name: Relevant Range
runners_data.note: Competitive prominent type who won over 8f on good ground; Elle-May Croot claims 5lb which is useful at the weights, but only 2W6P from 15 similar-going runs suggests he finds ways to not win even when placed handily.
runners_data.comment: Relevant Range won two starts back and returns after 32 days looking well-placed under 133 lb from stall 11, with experience of today's distance and going in his favour; a fourth last time out hints at consistency worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Rusheen Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins from five comparable efforts in similar going; Levey is a top rider and the 34-day break appears manageable given the horse's fitness history — strong place candidate if he tracks Volto closely.
runners_data.comment: Rusheen Boy sits bottom of the weights on 133 lb and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but consecutive fifth-place finishes in his last two starts make him hard to fancy, and ranked eleventh of fourteen on our figures, he faces a steep ask here.

runners_data.name: Soames Forsyte
runners_data.note: Naturally races held up but prior history shows a prominent tag (hg:p) suggesting connections have tried to move him forward; Eaves rides and the trainer has had three winners from 14 runners over the past fortnight, but the style redistribution into midfield means he is not truly in his best slot.
runners_data.comment: Soames Forsyte brings useful distance and going experience to this, and his our rating of 67 edges his official mark, suggesting he retains more ability than recent results imply; yet to win in his last six starts, that winless streak is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: Front-hoof placed in 6 of his last 15 fibresand-style runs without winning, carrying visor; Bradley rides and the horse's consistent placing record at 8f on similar going makes him a realistic frame candidate if he can sit just off the leader.
runners_data.comment: Bajan Bandit has been knocking at the door, finishing second twice and third in his last three starts, yet he remains winless in recent starts and faces stiff competition ranked eighth of fourteen. Experience over today's trip and going helps, and eleven days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Special Breeze
runners_data.note: Off for 103 days, which is the longest absence in the field; a natural hold-up horse shifted into midfield by the congested rear, and the combination of layoff, style mismatch and modest similar-going record (0W0P from 6) makes this a difficult each-way proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Special Breeze faces a stiff task; 103 days off the track adds another question mark, though she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Aim For The Bull
runners_data.note: Genuinely in-form horse with two wins in his last five runs including over this C&D trip on good ground; Hornby takes the ride and the prominent/pressing style suits this race shape well — one of the most interesting profiles in the race on paper.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well adrift of the field on our figures, Aim For The Bull faces a stiff task at these weights despite a sequence that includes back-to-back wins in his last two starts; he has run over today's trip and going, but 63 days off the track adds further uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Mr Fustic
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with strong fibresand knowledge (14/15 similar-going runs, 2W5P); a genuine hold-up horse by preference now mapped into midfield due to rear congestion, though his experience of the track and course means he knows how to find a run — Ghiani is a sharp judge in transit.
runners_data.comment: Mr Fustic won three starts back but has finished fourth and fifth since, and a 104-day absence makes fitness a concern; ranked 12 of 14 on our figures, he faces a stiff task from stall 10 under 127 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Volto di Medusa is the one confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Cieren Fallon can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over Southwell's flat fibresand mile. Just Typical, Rusheen Boy, Bajan Bandit, Relevant Range and Aim For The Bull will look to press into prominent positions behind the pacesetter, creating a defined mid-group contest rather than a true speed duel at the head of affairs. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Aspull, Soames Forsyte, Special Breeze and Mr Fustic are genuine closers redistributed into midfield slots because the back of the field is oversubscribed, and their ability to produce a true late run will be compromised by the race unfolding slower than their style demands. A controlled pace from a lone leader on standard fibresand over a mile heavily favours horses racing prominently or at worst in a close-tracking position, as the lack of genuine pace compression will leave late runners short of the acceleration they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Volto Dictates, Pace Test
scenarios.trigger: If Volto di Medusa bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair but unhurried tempo, allowing prominent chasers to fire off his back.
scenarios.body: Fallon slots Volto into a comfortable lead and the race develops into a test of who holds form into the final two furlongs from the front-running or close-tracking positions; horses who can sit just behind the leader and challenge entering the straight will be ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Just Typical, Rusheen Boy or Bajan Bandit push hard to sit on Volto's shoulder and inject genuine pressure through the middle part of the race.
scenarios.body: A contested tempo raises the sectionals, stretching the field out and making it harder for the front-runner to sustain; the race becomes a battle of prominent types with stamina and recent fitness rewarded.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Catches Them Napping
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely moderate and the field bunches, creating a wall of horses entering the home straight that gives closers a window.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo paradoxically allows a horse with a strong finishing kick to thread through a tightly packed group, but this requires the redistributed hold-up horses to have genuinely secured a rear position, which the crowded field makes difficult.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From The Gate
scenarios.trigger: If the large 14-runner field produces early crowding, forcing several prominent types to check or switch, disrupting planned tactical positions entirely.
scenarios.body: Disruption at the start scrambles the expected order and opens the race to a horse that gets a clean passage regardless of early positioning; course specialists and horses fresh from a break with tactical flexibility benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Volto di Medusa's unchallenged lead is the race's central axis — if Fallon elects to dawdle through the first four furlongs, the lack of true pace could compress the field into a sprint finish that his rivals will relish far more than a test of front-running stamina.

Aim For The Bull arrives on the back of two wins over this trip and is drawn to press early; if Hornby pushes forward assertively from the gate, he could apply more sustained pressure to Volto than anticipated and sharpen the pace significantly.

With Aspull, Soames Forsyte, Special Breeze and Mr Fustic all redistributed from their natural hold-up positions, the midfield section of this race will be unusually congested — watch for scrimmaging between the 6f and 4f markers where these horses are likely to find themselves squeezed.

Bajan Bandit's consistent placing record without winning (0W6P at 8f on similar going) is a flag — the visor suggests connections are trying to sharpen him up, and if the moderate early pace produces a steadily run race he could be the horse who finds a way to place again rather than convert.

Special Breeze returns after 103 days and is drawn in a field that gives very little opportunity for a horse needing a true strong gallop — monitor market moves late, as any significant support could signal the trainer has the horse ready, but on form and style grounds alone this is a watch rather than a follow.

races.name: Southwell Racecourse Conference & Events Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Mayflower Billy
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile on going he handles fine, but his AW form at this distance shows just one placing from six attempts on similar surfaces and he faces the same closing challenge as the rest of the rear group; 60 days off is a minor concern for a yard running at 1/3 over 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Mayflower Billy has been knocking on the door, with a second three starts back a clear highlight, but he has been winless in his last five and returns after a 60-day break, which is the key unknown heading into this.

runners_data.name: Silky Lass
runners_data.note: Prominent rider with a strong AW record at this course and trip — eight similar-going runs yielding one win and six places is a standout figure in this field — and Alex Jary's 3lb claim helps offset the weight; 64 days off is the one query.|
runners_data.comment: Silky Lass has distance and going experience in her favour, and her second two starts back shows she can get competitive, but a ninth last time out after 64 days off raises fitness questions as she returns from a break carrying 132 lb from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Power Strike
runners_data.note: Prominent type stepping back to a mile from 10f and returning after 144 days off, which is a significant freshness concern; Julie Camacho's yard has been quiet (0/15 over 14 days) and the limited form line on AW makes it hard to assess true capability at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Power Strike has run over today's trip and going, carries a workable weight of 131 lb from stall 5, and our rating of 72 marks him out as a genuine threat in a competitive field; the concern is a 144-day absence and a winless recent run of three starts.

runners_data.name: Wield
runners_data.note: Held-up or mid-division performer who has placed consistently at 7f on good ground but whose sole Southwell run (3rd at 7f, Standard) is the most relevant piece of form; headgear (t) noted, 11-day turnaround is a positive sign of fitness, and he is the most likely beneficiary if the front pair tire.|
runners_data.comment: Wield has run over today's trip and going, carries a manageable 135 lb from stall six, and our rating puts him ahead of his official mark, flagging genuine claims here; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts, with a seventh last time out the immediate worry.

runners_data.name: Filly Eilish
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner and likely to get an uncontested lead under De Sousa; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is largely moot here because she IS the pace, not racing against it — her AW win at this distance and 5/6 placed record on similar going underpin her chance.|
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back, and at 135 lb from stall one she arrives here fit on 25 days' rest with experience of today's trip and going — a filly worth siding with on current conditions.

runners_data.name: Legacy Rock
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose recent form includes back-to-back wins at 8f on good ground, but those came on turf and his limited AW exposure (0W0P from three) is a meaningful concern stepping onto this surface; headgear retained, 11-day turnaround suggests he is fit.|
runners_data.comment: Legacy Rock arrives here with back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and his experience over today's trip and going underlines his suitability, with our rating of 76 marking him out as the one to beat; the worry is that his last two runs have both been sixths, so he must show he has rediscovered that earlier spark.

runners_data.name: Test Run
runners_data.note: A natural closer by style whose true position is further back than the map shows — pushed into midfield by weight of hold-up numbers — making his task harder if Filly Eilish sets an unhurried pace; modest recent form (4-5-4 last three) and a yard running at 3/34 over 14 days does not inspire confidence.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Test Run faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and returns after a 30-day break, but his recent string of fourths and a fifth offers little encouragement at 130 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Dacres Cross
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's yard has been active (3/32) but this horse's form has been limited to 6-7f on good ground, meaning the step up to a mile on AW is an untested combination; his natural inclination to close from the rear is compromised by a field that leaves him without an ideal berth.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and without a run for 54 days, Dacres Cross arrives needing a fitness question answered, though he has run over today's trip and our rating of 72 suggests a shade more ability than his official mark implies.

runners_data.name: Vega Storm
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey in decent form (7/47), and Vega Storm has placed once from seven similar-going runs, but the redistribution away from the true rear means he is denied the holding position that suits his closer's style; 21-day turnaround looks fine for fitness.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Vega Storm faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns after a reasonable 21-day break carrying 128 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Sailor's Return
runners_data.note: David O'Meara sends out a consistent yard (3/39) but this horse has yet to win in six career runs and his best efforts have come at 7-8f on good ground rather than AW; naturally suited to a late run from off the pace, he is among those most compromised by the race's lack of genuine early pressure, and headgear (t) has not yet unlocked improvement.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Sailor's Return makes little appeal, though she has run over today's trip before and comes here fresh enough at 28 days since her last outing.

races.paceDynamic: Filly Eilish is the lone confirmed front-runner in this ten-runner 1m handicap and, with no genuine rival to pressure her from the gates, Silvestre De Sousa can control the tempo entirely on his own terms, setting a sustainable, gallop that shapes this race from the front. Silky Lass and Power Strike are the most likely prominent horses to sit just off her heels, but neither carries the early pace to disrupt Filly Eilish's rhythm, meaning the fractions should be measured and the race will not develop into a true test of stamina. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Test Run, Dacres Cross, Vega Storm and Sailor's Return are all natural closers redistributed into midfield positions, and without a genuine pace collapse they will struggle to generate the momentum needed to reel in a controlled front-runner. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace — those able to track Filly Eilish and respond in the straight — because a lone leader dictating at a fair but not punishing tempo will rarely be run down by true hold-up types operating out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Filly Eilish dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and De Sousa times the move to the straight perfectly, giving nothing away.
scenarios.body: Filly Eilish stamps her authority from flag to finish, with nothing to push her wide or quicken her early, and her solid AW record at this trip confirms she handles the surface; the prominent-tracking Silky Lass is best-placed to finish off a strong second if the winner has too much in reserve.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If Silky Lass or Power Strike push forward to sit tight on Filly Eilish's quarters and raise the tempo through the middle portion of the race.
scenarios.body: A competitive early duel develops that stretches the field and ensures a more genuine test for the front two, increasing the chance that a prominent or midfield type benefits from others' slightly elevated effort; Silky Lass's strong AW form at this course and trip makes her the most likely beneficiary if Filly Eilish is drawn into a contested lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses or leaders tire dramatically in the final two furlongs, handing an opening to the redistributed hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Wield, who has legitimate prominent-to-midfield credentials and has placed well recently, is best-placed among those mapping away from the front; the true hold-up types — Test Run, Dacres Cross, Vega Storm and Sailor's Return — face the compounded difficulty of racing out of role and needing a pace collapse that the lone-leader shape makes unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is entirely false, the field concertinas, and genuine closers get a sprint finish they can exploit.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Filly Eilish to overreach or the tempo to crawl to the point where the field has no gaps to fill; given that Test Run, Dacres Cross, Vega Storm and Sailor's Return are all racing well outside their natural position, this remains a low-probability outcome even if the pace does collapse.

watchPoints.text: Filly Eilish (De Sousa) breaks cleanly — if she leads unchallenged from the start, the race shape is effectively set and her price may be on the short side for what becomes a procession.

Silky Lass is the likeliest horse to test Filly Eilish's lead through the final three furlongs; watch whether Alex Jary commits to sitting just off the pace or gets pushed back — her position at the halfway point will be decisive.

Power Strike's 144-day layoff means a sluggish start or a sluggish early pitch is possible; if she misses the break or fails to press forward, the prominent plan collapses entirely and she becomes irrelevant to the shape.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Test Run, Dacres Cross, Vega Storm and Sailor's Return — will bunch through the middle of the race; watch for traffic issues in the straight if they all try to find the same gap at the same time.

Wield (Luke Morris) is the one midfield horse worth tracking from the three-furlong pole: if the pace does soften and gaps appear, his recent placed form and course experience make him the most credible late challenger from off the pace.

races.name: Southwell Racecourse Conference & Events Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Jackabi
runners_data.note: Headgear flag (hg:t) is a key angle for a 3yo on Standard Southwell; hold-up style means she faces the same midfield traffic issues as the pack, but her one win over 7f at Goodwood on good ground and a recent fourth suggest she retains ability — Rob Hornby booking worth noting and trainer Mark Rimell is 0/6 in the last 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Jackabi makes it hard to build a case, with a fourth last time out and only one win in his last five starts, though he has experience over today's trip and going, breaks from stall one, and returns on a fresh 25-day break.

runners_data.name: Wise Crack
runners_data.note: Shane Gray replaces a stronger jockey and Ruth Carr's 14-day strike rate of 1/23 is uninspiring; this is genuinely a hold-up performer whose position on the map understates how far back she will want to race — her one place on a previous visit to this track is the main form hook but being forced to race in midfield against her inclination is a meaningful negative.
runners_data.comment: Wise Crack franked his win two starts back with a fair fourth last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and going conditions. Fit enough at 21 days between runs, and a speed rating of 67 gives him a solid angle, though the trainer's recent strike rate is a concern.

runners_data.name: Ballybunion
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's yard is 2/17 in the last fortnight which is reasonable, and Callum Shepherd is a capable partner, but Ballybunion's last two wins were over 6f at Goodwood on good ground — the step to 8f on Fibresand is an unproven combination, and he is a true hold-up horse shuffled into midfield where he cannot be at his best.
runners_data.comment: Ballybunion has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating puts him second among nine here, suggesting he is a genuine threat despite being winless in his last five starts; that elusive first win remains the key question.

runners_data.name: Roi de Coeur
runners_data.note: The key horse in this race — one win and one place on Standard Southwell going in his last six starts (4/6 sim-going) confirms he handles the surface, and Marco Ghiani rides prominently by nature; lone front-runner who faces no credible challenger for the lead and Marco Botti is 3/17 in the 14-day window, a solid recent rate.
runners_data.comment: Roi de Coeur arrives on the back of a second two starts back and a win three starts back, boasting experience over today's trip and going, and our rating has him top-rated, if only narrowly — the chief question is whether that fifth last time out signals he's just past his peak.

runners_data.name: Taradif
runners_data.note: Sean Levey is a high-class booking for Jessica Macey whose stable is a modest 1/3 in the 14-day window; Taradif has placed at 8f and 10f on Standard Southwell, giving him a genuine course-and-distance angle, and his hold-up style suits a race where the front runner may be catchable if tracked correctly — 16 days since last run is fresh enough.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Taradif is hard to fancy at the weights, though he does bring distance and going experience and a third last time out offers a small crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Boy Named Sioux
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman takes the 3lb claim and Fahey's yard is in form at 7/47; Boy Named Sioux won over 8f on Standard and was placed over the same trip, so the trip and surface suit, but a hold-up style in a race this crowded at the rear and just nine days since last run may blunt his finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Boy Named Sioux arrives on a quick turnaround of nine days and an unplaced effort latest, though he has experience over today's trip and going and our rating edges him ahead of his official mark, offering some reason for cautious interest.

runners_data.name: Alkumatic Jo Jo
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado is 0/12 in the 14-day window which is a cold stat, though Silvestre De Sousa arriving in the saddle lifts the profile; with seven runs on Standard Southwell and three placed efforts, course familiarity is genuine — but this is a horse whose natural inclination to race at the rear will be frustrated by midfield placement, blunting his effectiveness.
runners_data.comment: Alkumatic Jo Jo was third last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a solid platform from stall three off 130 lb; the worry is that she has been winless in her last six starts, suggesting a win may still prove elusive.

runners_data.name: Kiani King
runners_data.note: Headgear flag (hg:t) and Hughie Morrison's yard 0/10 in the 14-day window are the headline angles; Billy Loughnane is a live jockey booking but Kiani King's best Southwell effort is a third over 8f and he has had 35 days off — the hold-up style compounded by a forced midfield berth makes this a low-probability scenario without a significant gear change.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Kiani King at least showed a return to form with a third last time out after a pair of poor efforts, and he has run over today's distance and going before; carrying 128 lb from stall four after a 35-day break, he may need to find more to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Hunterian
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's operation has placed four horses from 38 runners in the last fortnight, modest but not cold; Hunterian won over 8f on soft and was placed on soft twice — the jump to Standard Fibresand is a going question worth flagging — and his natural hold-up inclinations push him into the redistributed midfield group, though his recent winning form is the strongest raw ability claim among that group.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures and his speed rating of 58 trails the field, Hunterian has been sixth in each of his last two starts and is hard to fancy despite a win three starts back; experience over today's trip and going offers slim consolation.

races.paceDynamic: Roi de Coeur is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of nine and, with no rival likely to press him seriously from the outset, he can establish a comfortable, controlled lead through the early stages of this flat Fibresand mile at Southwell. The pace he sets will be honest but not punishing — a lone leader dictating from the front on Standard ground creates a rail-to-tape scenario where that lead position is genuinely difficult to peg back. The field behind him is dominated by hold-up types, but with five horses tagged as redistributed — Wise Crack, Ballybunion, Alkumatic Jo Jo, Kiani King, and Hunterian all displaced from their true rear-of-field position — there is a genuine glut of horses who will be forced to race closer than ideal, crowding midfield and reducing the clean air available to true late-runners. This race shape strongly favours Roi de Coeur and any horse capable of tracking him in second or third early, as the bunched midfield will create traffic problems and the front runner is unlikely to be run down by horses racing out of their natural role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Roi de Coeur Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Roi de Coeur is allowed to dictate from the front without any credible challenger pressing him through the bend.
scenarios.body: He settles into a rhythm on the front end, controls the tempo, and has enough in reserve to repel challengers off the final turn; his OR-70 mark and one win plus one place at Southwell on Standard going underline his suitability.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sits second or third at a comfortable distance from Roi de Coeur and times a run to collar him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A patient tracker benefits from the even tempo set by the lone leader, staying on the bridle longer than hold-up horses buried in traffic; Taradif's recent third at Goodwood and Sean Levey booking give him the profile, while Jackabi has the hg:t headgear flag and a winning run over this trip to recommend her.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Crowded Midfield Breaks Free
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched pack of redistributed hold-up types splits on the home straight and one finds a decisive gap late.
scenarios.body: With five horses forced into midfield against their natural style, the group will be compact turning for home and any runner with the class to quicken through narrow spaces could emerge; Hunterian's recent win and two SOF places show ability, and Alkumatic Jo Jo's three places on this surface give them each an outside chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sweep Materialises
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses unexpectedly or Roi de Coeur is checked, handing a late run to genuine closers.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Roi de Coeur to fail in his role AND for displaced hold-up horses to find clear passage — both unlikely given the controlled Standard going and traffic conditions; Ballybunion's two wins at 6f at Goodwood show raw ability but he is operating out of role and on unfavoured terms here.

watchPoints.text: Watch Roi de Coeur's early stride — if he jumps cleanly and Marco Ghiani allows him to bowl along unchallenged, his ability to control tempo from the front could make him very hard to catch on Standard Southwell going with no pace rival in the field.

Monitor midfield traffic turning for home: with five horses (Wise Crack, Ballybunion, Alkumatic Jo Jo, Kiani King, Hunterian) all compressed into the same mid-division band, interference or a narrow run off the final bend is a material risk that could affect the finish order.

Taradif and Jackabi are the two horses most likely to find a tracking position close enough to Roi de Coeur to benefit from the controlled pace — watch whether Levey and Hornby commit early to a second or third slot rather than dropping in with the hold-up pack.

Hunterian's going profile (wins and places on soft/good-to-soft) relative to today's Standard Fibresand surface is worth monitoring in the pre-race market — if he drifts, it may reflect trainer or market concern about the surface switch after 45 days off.

races.name: Gents Evening Saturday 24th October Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sole Spirit
runners_data.note: Returned from a 354-day absence and won on this exact course and distance on Standard Fibresand; form string of 1161 is eye-catching, but that layoff and the hold-up style — genuine but functional here — make him an each-way proposition rather than a banker.
runners_data.comment: Sole Spirit returns from a lengthy 354-day absence, which makes him very hard to trust despite a sharp recent profile of three wins in his last four starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, but ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, he faces a stiff task on reappearance.

runners_data.name: Cairdeas
runners_data.note: Placed twice in last five starts but never wins; placed at OR=67 twice on Standard Southwell previously yet seems to lack a finishing kick to convert; Tom Eaves holds the booking but a consistent without winning profile limits upside.
runners_data.comment: Cairdeas has finished second twice in his last five starts and returns on a freshening break of 25 days with experience of today's trip and going, and our rating of 74 marks him as a genuine threat in this field; the risk is he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Dicko The Legend
runners_data.note: Recent 14-day turnaround for the Liam Bailey yard; true hold-up horse by nature that has been pushed into a midfield slot by race shape — with five consecutive placings between 3rd and 6th, consistency is his calling card but winning is elusive in this configuration.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out but winless in his last six starts, Dicko The Legend has experience of today's trip and going and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround; drawing stall one and carrying 131 lb are the weights to factor in.

runners_data.name: Hectic
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie, trained by Liam Bailey alongside stablemate Dicko The Legend on a 14-day spin; naturally wants to come from off the pace but the compressed field means he cannot get to the back — his one Southwell win on Standard is a tick but the style fit is imperfect here.
runners_data.comment: Hectic was third two starts back and returns on a quick turnaround of just 14 days, bringing distance and going experience to the table; our rating of 74 marks him out as a leading danger, though he remains winless in recent starts and will need to find more from stall five.

runners_data.name: Baba Reza
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old equipped with a pear (pea ring) running prominently when conditions suit; three placings from six Southwell starts suggest course affinity, but the 0 from 15 win record at this handicap level on Standard going is a persistent concern even if he lands closer to the front than usual today.

runners_data.name: Jesse Luc
runners_data.note: Southwell specialist — 14 of his last 15 runs have been on Standard fibresand and he has won twice and placed six times on this surface; Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim combined with the tongue-tie is notable, but his natural hold-up style is squeezed by the field shape.
runners_data.comment: Jesse Luc arrives here winless in his last six starts, with a seventh last time out and a sixth two starts back suggesting a horse that keeps finding a handful in front of him; a third three starts back hints at ability, however, and he has experience over today's trip and going, carrying 129 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Thunderous Love
runners_data.note: Front-running pear gear confirmed, placed twice at Goodwood recently; OR=63 gives her a weight advantage over the top weights, and a prominent pitch suits this race shape perfectly — the jockey Rob Hornby should be able to hold second or third behind Marianne Mozart.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with a pair of seconds her only consolation, Thunderous Love has run over today's trip and going before, but ranked 11 of 12 on our figures she faces a stiff task from stall 8 off 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Obsessor
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's four-year-old has placed twice at 5f on Standard going; naturally wants to come from off the pace but is mapped into midfield by race density — the step up to 6f from recent 5f runs may not help, and the style compromise is a genuine concern.
runners_data.comment: Fantasy Obsessor has shown ability in recent starts, second three starts back, but has been disappointing in her last two outings and remains yet to win in recent form; experience over today's trip and going offers some hope, though her rating of 70 leaves her with plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Classy Clarets
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the field at OR=70 and has won four of his last six, including a Southwell win on Standard; Shay Farmer's 5lb claim is a bonus and a prominent style is perfectly suited to this race shape — sits as the standout profile horse today.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom three on our figures and rated below his official mark, Classy Clarets faces a stiff ask, though his recent sequence — second last time out after four wins in his last six — at least signals he arrives in fine fettle, with distance and going experience adding modest encouragement.

runners_data.name: Hierarchy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with 12 Southwell runs on Standard going, winning twice; William Carver rides and the tongue-tie (tb) is retained; a hold-up horse who consistently hits the frame here but struggles to win — form of 034065 shows frustrating consistency without a recent win.
runners_data.comment: Hierarchy has run over today's trip and going and shaped with enough promise to earn a top rating among these twelve, and at 135 lb from stall 12, he goes into this fresh enough on a 16-day break — though yet to win in recent starts, he is the one to side with.

runners_data.name: Marianne Mozart
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner ridden by Silvestre De Sousa; five runs have all produced 5th-place finishes on Standard going including Southwell, meaning the form book is modest, but uncontested lead-setting on this sharp straight track is her one genuine weapon.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Marianne Mozart faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's distance and going before and 31 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Travel Agent
runners_data.note: Equipped with hood and a sheepskin noseband; trained by Adam Kirby, who is better known as a jockey, on a 14-day turnaround; three wins from nine Southwell runs on Standard going show course aptitude, but the hold-up style is compromised by the crowded rear and the OR=68 puts him in a competitive spot.
runners_data.comment: Travel Agent has experience over today's trip and ground, and his second in recent starts offers some encouragement, but he has been winless in his last six outings and that sequence of fifths and sevenths suggests he is capable of mixing it midfield rather than threatening at the finish.

races.paceDynamic: Marianne Mozart is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Silvestre De Sousa should be able to dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop across the 6f Southwell straight. Thunderous Love and Classy Clarets will press forward into prominent positions just behind, but neither is a true pace-setter, meaning the early tempo is likely to be modest rather than scorching. The field contains a heavy concentration of hold-up types — Hectic, Dicko The Legend, Baba Reza, Jesse Luc, Fantasy Obsessor and others are genuine closers who cannot all get to the rear naturally and have been redistributed toward midfield, compressing the pack behind Marianne Mozart and reducing the likelihood of a true end-to-end test. With a sustainable gallop and the pack bunched behind, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently — Classy Clarets and Thunderous Love are best placed to track the leader and pounce, while the genuine hold-up horses, squeezed into midfield, face a compromised passage and are racing partially out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Marianne Mozart Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Marianne Mozart dictates an uncontested lead and the moderate pace holds, setting up a finish for those in her slipstream.
scenarios.body: Marianne Mozart bowls along without pressure and the race becomes a test of class and positioning over the final 2f; horses prominent throughout and able to quicken off the steady tempo are best served.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pounce At Two
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to string the field out but not kill the front-runner, and those in second/third positions produce their finishing effort early.
scenarios.body: Classy Clarets, carrying top weight but in exceptional recent form with four wins, can sit in behind and deliver a strong challenge from 2f out; Thunderous Love's recent placed form at Goodwood shows she handles a fair gallop and can produce a late surge from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens enough in the middle stages to weaken the leaders and allow redistributed closers to finish through on the stands rail.
scenarios.body: This is the least natural scenario given how many true hold-up types are compressed into midfield and racing out of role; Sole Spirit is the one hold-up horse with genuine winning form at Southwell on similar going and carries the best credentials if this shape materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pairs
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so modest that the front pair simply hold on without being challenged and the closers never get organised in time.
scenarios.body: With a low-key tempo and Marianne Mozart setting her own terms, neither the genuine hold-up horses nor the midfield pack can generate the momentum to reel in the leaders; this outcome is unlikely but possible if the field is strung out very late.

watchPoints.text: Classy Clarets is the form horse of the race — four wins from six — and a prominent style slots perfectly into this pace shape; watch whether Shay Farmer settles him just behind Marianne Mozart and produces him at the 2f pole.

Marianne Mozart has not won in three starts and has finished 5th every time, so while she controls the pace, watch whether De Sousa allows the tempo to drop so low that the race turns into a sprint finish she cannot hold off.

The Liam Bailey double-runner combination of Dicko The Legend and Hectic merits scrutiny — both are true hold-up horses racing out of role today, and their redistribution into midfield means stable tactics could influence how either runs if they are used to assist each other.

Sole Spirit returns from 354 days off with a win at Southwell already on his record; watch his pre-race market move, as any significant support would suggest connections are confident the layoff is not a concern.

Jesse Luc's 14-of-15 runs on Standard fibresand mark him as the most course-experienced hold-up horse in the field — if the pace quickens mid-race and gaps open, his track knowledge under Tom Kiely-Marshall's claim makes him a shape-dependent outsider to monitor.
